newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden inflation still seen falling - Riksbank poll.
newsitem.headline: Sweden inflation still seen falling - Riksbank poll.

text.p: Swedish inflation expectations are still falling, a survey commissioned by the central Riksbank, showed on Wednesday.
The survey by economic research institute Prospera AB showed annualised inflation in one year's time is seen at 1.7 percent, in two years at 1.9 percent, and in five years at 2.2 percent.
Prospera's last poll in May showed average inflation expectations had fallen to 2.3 percent in one year, 2.4 percent in two year and 2.7 percent in five years.

The survey, carried out four times a year, is one of the central bank's key analytical tools used in its policy planning and is considered one of the weightiest in Sweden when it comes to forecasting inflation.
The poll involves a sample group of money market players, purchasing managers, and representatives of employees' and employers' organisations.

The money market expections were 1.8 percent in one year (2.0 percent), 2.0 percent in two years (2.2 percent), and 2.3 percent in five years (2.5 percent). The Riksbank is due to present its next inflation report on September 24.
